request:
Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should only desk staff be able to mark an item as claimed (for example with a password), or can anyone using the board do it?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When an item is claimed, should the owner's name be visible to everyone viewing the board, or only to desk staff?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should the desk be able to edit or remove items, for example a wrong report or an item never collected?
A: Not needed for now.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built the lost-and-found board in `app.py`. Items are saved in a file called `lost_and_found.db` in the project folder. I also wrote 13 automated tests covering every request you made and every rule, and they all pass.

**What the board can do:**
- **`POST /items`** reports a found item. You send `description`, `where_found` and `date_found` (written as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2024-03-10). The board gives the item a number automatically and marks it "waiting". It refuses the report if any of the three details is missing or blank, or if the date isn't a real date (2024-02-30, for example, is refused).
- **`GET /items`** shows every item on the board.
- **`GET /items/waiting`** shows only the items still waiting for their owners.
- **`GET /items/{item number}`** shows one item with all its details.
- **`POST /items/{item number}/claim`** marks an item as claimed. You send `owner_name`, and it's refused if the name is missing or blank. If the item has already been claimed, it's refused with an "already claimed" message and the first owner's name stays as it was.

If someone looks up or claims an item number that doesn't exist, they get a "not found" message.

**Choices I made where you had no preference:**
- Anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed. There's no password.
- The owner's name is shown with the item's other details, so everyone viewing the board can see it.
- Items can't be edited or removed, as you asked.

**Two questions for later:**
- Would you like only desk staff to be able to mark items as claimed?
- For privacy, would you prefer owners' names to be hidden from the public board?

plan.summary: A simple online board for the campus lost-and-found desk. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description, where it was found and the date it was found. Everyone can see all items, look at one item, or see only the items still waiting for their owners. When an owner collects an item, it is marked as claimed and the owner's name is written down; an item cannot be claimed twice. As you had no preference, we chose the simplest options: anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed (no password), and the owner's name is shown along with the item like the rest of its details. Editing or removing items is left out, as you asked. Questions for you: would you later like only desk staff to be able to mark items as claimed? And for privacy, would you prefer owners' names to be hidden from the public board?

data.name: Item
fields: Item number (given automatically by the board)
Description: a short description of the item (required)
Where found: the place the item was found (required)
Date found: the day the item was found (required)
Owner's name: written down when the item is claimed (empty until then)

endpoints.does: Reports a found item with its description, where it was found and the date it was found. It starts as 'waiting'.
Shows all items on the board.
Shows only the items that are still waiting for their owners.
Shows one item and all its details.
Marks the item as claimed and writes down the owner's name.

rules: A report is refused if the description, where it was found or the date found is missing.
A report is refused if the date found is not a real date.
Claiming is refused if the owner's name is missing.
Claiming is refused if the item has already been claimed.
Looking at or claiming an item that does not exist is refused with a 'not found' message.
